segments.summary: Rowe asks if improvisation must be jazz; Jordan tells of a shy girl on flutaphone who improvised once she began.

segments.title: Crowley family, Professor O'Jay and Illinois Jacquet
segments.summary: Jordan's family was not very musical; his teacher Professor O'Jay taught Illinois Jacquet, and Jacquet's honking and screaming opened Jordan to playing free and high notes.

segments.title: High-note fingerings and clarinet study with Alvin Batiste
segments.summary: Jordan worked out altissimo fingerings in high school, was made to play clarinet at college beside Batiste, and took the pads off his saxophone.

segments.title: Soprano out of favor; coming up on Bird
segments.summary: Old sopranos were given away; Jordan skipped Bechet's generation and came up listening to Charlie Parker.

segments.title: Swing broadcasts heard as a boy
segments.summary: Sneaking the radio to hear Woody Herman, Basie and Ellington late at night.

segments.title: Evan Thomas, the Crowley trumpeter Armstrong feared
segments.summary: Local legend of Evan Thomas, a Crowley trumpeter said to scare Louis Armstrong, killed before Jordan was born.

segments.chapter: Sessions and teaching in New Orleans
segments.title: Choosing teaching over full-time performing
segments.summary: Jordan chose education, has taught and played all his life with seven kids, and tells students to get a degree; he drifted into R&B work as second tier behind the top New Orleans session players.

segments.chapter: Sessions and teaching in New Orleans
segments.title: Second-tier R&B session work in New Orleans
segments.summary: How the sessions worked: head arrangements, live takes, overtime tricks, baritone playing bass lines before electric bass, and union pay of forty to fifty dollars.

segments.chapter: Sessions and teaching in New Orleans
segments.title: Sessions versus a high-school teaching job
segments.summary: Missing school days after late sessions and calling the school board's bluff because his band was so good.

segments.chapter: Sessions and teaching in New Orleans
segments.title: Teaching high-school students by letting them hear him practice
segments.summary: Jordan practiced where students could hear him and wrote lines for them; several became serious saxophonists.

segments.chapter: Sessions and teaching in New Orleans
segments.title: Raising his own children on the instrument
segments.summary: His kids heard him and Alvin Batiste practice; he wanted them to have solid technique, and Kent, Marlon and Rachel played classical solos and attended Tanglewood and Eastman.

segments.title: Reeds, mouthpieces and how he practices
segments.summary: Fighting with bad reeds, shaving mouthpieces, and playing off drum pitches on the bandstand rather than practicing jazz.

segments.title: The William Parker trio session and its titles
segments.summary: Jordan expected a knock-out session but the others brought bells and gongs; the producer named the tracks, including the chicken wings voiceover.

segments.title: Katrina and the album's turbulent passages
segments.summary: A reviewer linked the album to Katrina; Jordan says the forces were his fellow musicians and tells of a more powerful Brooklyn club gig.

segments.title: Late Coltrane, Pharaoh Sanders and Alvin Thomas playing through illness
segments.summary: Jordan on Trane's late playing and the Olatunji Center date, then Alvin Thomas playing on despite cancer; Rowe adds Lionel Hampton.

segments.title: Free playing needs technique and hearing; Bird's chord notes
segments.summary: Free playing is no excuse for lacking technique or ear; Jordan describes how Bird used upper tones rather than spelling chords.

segments.title: Playing the sound of the song, not the changes
segments.summary: Jordan argues he plays the sound of a tune rather than spelling chords; Bird versus Sonny Stitt and the piano influence on saxophone.

segments.title: Ornette says Jordan plays like a bass player
segments.summary: Ornette's alto-clef idea and his remark, after hearing Jordan's altissimo harmonics, that he sounds like a bass player.

segments.title: College listening to Ives and Cage; last seeing Armstrong
segments.summary: At college Jordan listened to Ives, Cage and Stockhausen while friends held a jam session, and once left a Cage concert to see Armstrong.

segments.title: Improvising with birds, lawn mowers and children's sounds
segments.summary: Jordan plays off ambient sounds, says he only wants to improvise whatever the label; Rowe mentions Parker and birds, and Jordan's kids recorded birds.

segments.title: The Niger session in Berlin with Buddy Collette and Bluiett
segments.summary: Hearing a recording on which he played contrabass clarinet; the theme was notated, played only at Joe Papp's theatre and in Berlin.

segments.title: Playing avant-garde in New Orleans: the last free man
segments.summary: Jordan calls it terrible; he started the IAQ with Alvin Fielder, was uninvited from the jazz festival, and has communities elsewhere including the AACM.

segments.title: Music that demands the listener: Stockhausen, Coltrane and pop
segments.summary: Jordan gave Stockhausen a piece played over his music; says serious music is not made to be accepted like pop.

segments.title: Swing as dance music versus listening music
segments.summary: Bird ended dancing; jazz is like twentieth-century classical music, and orchestras rarely play it.

segments.title: Twelve-tone practice as ear training
segments.summary: Jordan practices atonal twelve-tone lines as ear training, but only plays what fits what he hears.

segments.title: Making a living in jazz and the loss of record labels
segments.summary: Get a day job or a degree; few reach Herbie Hancock's level and labels no longer keep rosters, as Impulse once did for Coltrane.

segments.title: Cannonball played by ear
segments.summary: After Rowe's Coltrane 'Om' anecdote, Jordan says Cannonball heard changes by ear and sounded like a first alto player.

segments.title: Cannonball and the Batiste soprano piece in New Orleans
segments.summary: Cannonball played Batiste's written soprano part with Jordan covering, then promised to play some of Jordan's crazy stuff.

segments.title: Cannonball's horns and hearing versus practicing changes
segments.summary: His King Super 20 then Selmer, and how Cannonball heard rather than practiced changes.

segments.title: Cannonball and Nat Adderley as people
segments.summary: Cannonball was happy-go-lucky and friends with Batiste; Nat was the stable business one.

segments.title: Bert Robinson, Cannonball and how Kidd got his name
segments.summary: Hearing Bert Robinson jam with Cannonball at Florida A&M, and how Jordan got the name Kidd with two Ds.

segments.title: What to teach at jazz camps; Marlon's lesson
segments.summary: Jordan wants technical work, playing by ear and unison writing; he refused to write Marlon a solo so he would learn to hear it.

segments.title: Letting students stumble versus ready-made lessons
segments.summary: Schools hand students everything; Jordan thinks stumbling leads to new ideas, and imitation of Brecker or Coltrane is not arrival.

segments.title: Who last changed jazz?
segments.summary: Sam Rivers, Cecil Taylor, William Parker, Alan Silva and Monk named; he doesn't hear many records.

segments.title: Playing Broadway shows and singers' acts in New Orleans
segments.summary: Contracting and playing with visiting singers and shows at the Fairmont Blue Room.

segments.title: Collecting and losing instruments in the flood
segments.summary: Jordan's horns, bass clarinets and Super 20 saxophones, many lost to the flood.

segments.title: Evacuating to Baton Rouge; the flooded house
segments.summary: Evacuating to Alvin Batiste's house and the state of his flooded home.

segments.title: Taking no credit for students' success
segments.summary: He won't take credit for students who succeeded; some did not get breaks, like Cannonball before Miles.

segments.title: Skills for today's students; learning from mistakes in elementary band
segments.summary: Students should write and score; Jordan lets children's scale mistakes lead to Lydian sounds.

segments.title: The singing girl on the CD cover; 51 years in education
segments.summary: Jordan taught a bashful girl 'Mary Had a Little Lamb' on the day of the session; Rowe congratulates him on 51 years in education.

segments.title: Old New Orleans musical families
segments.summary: The Humphreys, Adamses and Bocages, plus M. Red Thompson who played with Hampton.

segments.chapter: New Orleans families, lifestyle and retirement
segments.title: Discouraging his kids from jazz and warning about the lifestyle
segments.summary: He steered his kids to classical, warns students of drug temptations, and says the slow people make it.

segments.title: Closing words of wisdom
segments.summary: Rowe thanks Jordan for his wisdom, who invites more questions.
